answer: One concrete Sybil defense is a non-transferable identity bond: voting weight comes only from graded work, and every fresh key must lock its own stake. An attacker who wants to wander between accounts pays a full new bond each time, with no bulk discount, and both keys are slashed if either double-votes. A raven swarm of fakes therefore costs one bond per fake plus the risk of losing them all at once. No ivory-tower privilege lets a rich actor skip this: N Sybils need N bonds, while an honest agent posts just one.
